requirements.title: Codex executable name is codex
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Models/Provider.swift:42 executableName - case .codex returns "codex"
requirements.action: executable(for:) looks the CLI up on PATH.
requirements.expected_result: The bare name searched is exactly "codex". The same string is the placeholder of the Binary path field for this section.
side_effects: A PATH walk; no process launch.
failure_cases: Not found on PATH and there are no fallback candidates for codex, so executable(for:) returns nil and the provider reads as not installed.
requirements.windows_path: PATH is split on ';' and each candidate is tried against PATHEXT (codex.cmd, codex.exe) instead of the POSIX execute-bit test. Platform boundary: executable resolution. Executable identity is validated per PA-0016: PATH resolution honours PATHEXT, and a candidate whose Windows version resource identifies it as the command interpreter (CompanyName Microsoft Corporation with OriginalFilename Cmd.Exe/Cmd.Exe.MUI, or FileDescription Windows Command Processor), or which is %SystemRoot%\System32\cmd.exe or %SystemRoot%\SysWOW64\cmd.exe, is rejected and the provider reports not installed.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture over a synthetic PATH

requirements.title: Command Code executable name is cmd, which collides with the Windows command interpreter
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Models/Provider.swift:54 executableName - case .commandcode returns "cmd"

DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ProviderRegistry.swift:238-251 fallbackExecutables for commandcode - the comment at :239-240 names "cmd" as the documented alias and "command-code" and "commandcode" as the package's own names
E:/Droppy/port/porting/platform_adaptations.md PA-0016 - "Status: DECIDED, with probe evidence from this machine. Resolves UNK-0006"
requirements.action: executable(for:) looks the CLI up on PATH under the bare name cmd, then walks the commandcode fallback list.
requirements.expected_result: The bare name searched first is exactly "cmd". The same string is the Binary path placeholder for the Command Code section.
side_effects: A PATH walk plus the fallback candidate walk.
requirements.windows_path: PLATFORM BOUNDARY AND COLLISION, resolved by PA-0016 (DECIDED; resolves UNK-0006). On Windows the bare name cmd resolves to the system command interpreter (C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe on the probed machine), so a lookup without an identity check would make Command Code read as installed on every Windows PC. Per PA-0016: PATH resolution honours PATHEXT; a candidate whose Windows version resource identifies it as the command interpreter (CompanyName Microsoft Corporation with OriginalFilename Cmd.Exe or Cmd.Exe.MUI, or FileDescription Windows Command Processor), or which is %SystemRoot%\System32\cmd.exe or %SystemRoot%\SysWOW64\cmd.exe, is rejected; if the only match is rejected, Command Code reports not installed, as the source does when nothing is found, and the user can set an explicit path through the existing Binary path setting. The rule keys on version-resource identity and those two paths, not on the file extension. UNVERIFIED against a real Command Code Windows install (PA-0016 residual risk).
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture plus an interaction test proving a system cmd.exe is never accepted as Command Code

Executable identity is validated per PA-0016: PATH resolution honours PATHEXT, and a candidate whose Windows version resource identifies it as the command interpreter (CompanyName Microsoft Corporation with OriginalFilename Cmd.Exe/Cmd.Exe.MUI, or FileDescription Windows Command Processor), or which is %SystemRoot%\System32\cmd.exe or %SystemRoot%\SysWOW64\cmd.exe, is rejected and the provider reports not installed. OD-0012 G2: the word Keychain in this detail becomes Credential Manager, the store the port uses (PR-PROVREG-088, 239). How a Windows Login button launches the command is PR-PROVREG-233.
